title: Refund claims for a delayed project - success rate and timelines
p1:
A delayed project does not always mean you automatically get your money back.

Many people assume that missing a deadline is enough to win a refund claim. The reality is usually more complicated.
p2: The surprising part? A large number of refund claims fail not because the delay was small, but because there is no clear proof of what was promised, when it was due, and how the delay affected the customer.
p3:
Success often depends on the contract terms, communication records, payment history, and whether the delay is considered a reasonable failure or a serious breach. Some claims may be resolved within weeks through negotiation, while formal disputes can take months or longer.

The practical lesson: save agreements, emails, invoices, and deadline commitments from the beginning. Strong evidence often matters more than frustration alone.
